templates.name: Recall → Explain → Transfer
templates.description: Recall the key concepts, explain one case, then apply the same reasoning to a second case.

templates.name: Recall → Explain
templates.description: A shorter activity built around a single case.

templates.name: Explain → Assess → Transfer
templates.description: Adds a recorded assessment question before the second case.

templates.name: Interview → Explain
templates.description: Students question the patient before explaining the case.

templates.name: Explain → Reflect
templates.description: One case discussion followed by a short reflection.

strategies.name: Hints first
strategies.description: Guiding questions and small hints before any correction.
strategies.instruction: Respond with a guiding question or a small hint; correct only after several unsuccessful attempts.

strategies.name: Direct correction
strategies.description: Says what was wrong and why, then checks understanding.
strategies.instruction: Say briefly what was right and what was wrong, give the correct explanation, then ask one check question.

strategies.name: No help
strategies.description: No hints or corrections until the end.
strategies.instruction: Acknowledge each answer neutrally; give no hints or corrections.

strategies.name: Short summary
strategies.description: One strength and one point to work on.
strategies.instruction: Give one short paragraph: one strength, then one concrete point to work on.

strategies.name: Concept checklist
strategies.description: One line per key concept with a short verdict.
strategies.instruction: List each key concept on its own line with a short verdict on how well it was explained.

strategies.name: Self-rating first
strategies.description: The student rates their own understanding before the feedback.
strategies.instruction: Before giving feedback, ask the student to rate their understanding from 1 to 5.

strategies.name: Forthcoming patient
strategies.instruction: Answer the student's questions clearly and completely.

strategies.name: Worried patient
strategies.instruction: Sound anxious; give fuller answers when the student is reassuring.

strategies.name: Reserved patient
strategies.description: Brief answers; details only when asked precisely.
strategies.instruction: Give brief answers; share details only when asked precise questions.

strategies.name: Badges
strategies.description: A badge for each key concept explained well.
strategies.instruction: At the end, list a badge for each key concept the student explained well.

welcome.label: Welcome message
welcome.text: Welcome! In this activity you will work through a clinical case with a virtual tutor. You can ask for feedback at any time. Ready to start?

welcome.label: Opening question
welcome.text: How would you explain this patient’s presentation?

know.label: Phase introduction
know.text: Acknowledge {{welcome.answer}} in one sentence without judging it, then introduce a short review of the key concepts.

know.label: Opening question
know.text: Which concepts do you need to explain this case?

know.label: Knowledge dialogue
know.text:
Review the key concepts in {{knowledge}} with the student, one open question at a time.
End when the main concepts have been recalled, or after six exchanges.

explain.label: Phase introduction
explain.text: Announce {{phase.name}} and invite the student to explain the case in their own words. One or two sentences.

explain.label: Opening question
explain.text: Explain the patient’s presentation in your own words.

explain.label: Case discussion
explain.text:
Discuss {{case1.vignette}} with the student and compare each answer with {{case1.expert}}, one missing point at a time, without giving the whole explanation. Allow up to {{level.hints}} hints per point.
End when the main points are covered, or after eight exchanges.

assess.label: Assessment question
assess.note: The answer is recorded for analysis; the tutor does not react to it.

transfer.label: Phase introduction
transfer.text: Close the previous case in one sentence and introduce a new patient who tests the same reasoning.

transfer.label: Opening question
transfer.text: Explain this patient’s presentation in your own words.

transfer.label: Case discussion
transfer.text:
Discuss {{case{N}.vignette}} with the student and compare each answer with {{case{N}.expert}}, one missing point at a time, without giving the whole explanation. Allow up to {{level.hints}} hints per point.
End when the main points are covered, or after eight exchanges.

interview.label: Instructions
interview.text: You can now talk to the patient. Ask whatever you need to understand the case.

interview.label: Patient role-play
interview.text:
Play the patient described in {{case1.vignette}}, in everyday language. Reveal items from {{case1.findings}} only when the student asks about them directly, and never suggest a diagnosis.
End when the student says they are ready, or after ten questions.

reflect.label: Reflection prompt
reflect.text: Looking back, which part of the reasoning was hardest for you, and why?

final.label: Personal feedback
final.text: Using {{transcript}} and {{evaluator.log}}, give the student brief feedback in {{student.language}}: what went well, then the step where they needed most help.

final.label: Review materials
final.text: Below are the cases, their explanations and the knowledge text for you to review.

assist.system: You help a medical educator author a virtual patient activity in which an LLM tutor guides a student through clinical cases. Reply with only the requested text: no preamble, no quotes, no markdown headings.

modes.text: Write the text the student will read for this element, exactly as it should appear.
modes.vignette: Write a case presentation (vignette) for this case: a realistic patient presentation with history, examination and key laboratory results, about 100 words, labs listed at the end. Do not state the diagnosis.
modes.prompt: Write the instructions an LLM follows for this element. Use {{fields}} from the available list where useful. For an interaction, include when the conversation should end (an exit condition) on its own final line.
modes.vprompt: Write instructions for an LLM that generates a new case vignette for this activity. Use {{fields}} from the available list where useful. Ask for about 100 words, labs listed at the end, and no diagnosis.
modes.expert: Write the expert explanation of this case: the reasoning a strong student should reach, as short numbered points linking the findings to the underlying mechanisms. Base it on the knowledge text and the case vignette.

preview.system: You produce short preview samples of what a student will see in a virtual patient activity. Follow the author's prompt and strategies faithfully, at the given student level. Never mention that this is a sample.
preview.generated: Write the text this prompt would produce for the student.
preview.interaction: Write a short sample exchange (two to four turns, starting with the student) that this prompt would produce. Put each turn on its own line, prefixed with STUDENT:, TUTOR: or PATIENT:.
preview.final_feedback: Write the final feedback this prompt would produce, for a student who did reasonably well but needed help in one step.
